ai.description: This gecko reaches 14 cm in snout-vent length. It is brownish-grey with dark, irregular dorsal spots and a series of enlarged, trihedral tubercles. The toes possess undivided subdigital lamellae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hemidactylus maculatus* is best distinguished by its large, prominent, and strongly keeled dorsal tubercles, which are arranged in 16–20 distinct longitudinal rows.
ai.habitat: *Hemidactylus maculatus* inhabits rocky outcrops, caves, and old buildings in dry deciduous forests and scrublands, ranging from sea level up to 1,200 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Leaf-toed Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt insects on rock faces and tree trunks while utilizing its adhesive toe pads to navigate.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hemidactylus maculatus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding typically occurs during the monsoon season, from June to September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Hemidactylus maculatus* is endemic to the Western Ghats and parts of the Deccan Plateau in India, typically inhabiting rocky areas from sea level to 1,500 meters.
